El dato concreto llega en el beat 2, antes del segundo 3, asi que el 'prime' se conserva. Marcas de chisme en el texto, no en la voz: posesivo redundante, cifras que nadie contaria (140 personas, cuatro cenas), y el aparte que solo daria alguien que estuvo alli (el bolso con los dos brazos). Giro fair-play con CINCO pistas plantadas antes de la revelacion: viene sola, el marido 'aparcando', no coge a la nina, el bolso agarrado, se va antes de comer. La linea de que se prometio en la fiesta de compromiso de mi hermana hace doble trabajo: justifica la rabia del narrador Y es la misdireccion. El loop es el mejor de la sesion: cierra en 'siempre la empiezo igual' y el reinicio del video ES ella empezandola otra vez.
script: She waited until the priest was actually pouring the water. Then she stood up, in the second row, and announced she was pregnant. A hundred and forty people turned around. My daughter was eleven weeks old, in my grandmother's christening gown, and every face in that church was pointed at my cousin Nadia. The priest stopped. He actually stopped, with the water still in his hand. And I thought, of course. Of course she did. Because that is who she is. She got engaged at my sister's engagement party. That is a real thing that happened, ask anyone in my family. So I was ready for this one. What I did not clock at the time was that she came alone. Her husband did not come. She said he was parking. He was not parking. And she did not hold my daughter. Everybody held her that day. Nadia stood by the font with her handbag hooked over both arms, like she was on a train, and she did not hold her, and she left before the food. My aunt told me in November. She said, you know she sat in the car park for twenty minutes before she came in. Nadia had been trying for three years. Two rounds, twenty two thousand dollars, nothing. Nobody told me, because I was pregnant that entire time and they were being kind, and being kind is how you end up the last person in a room to know anything. She had a scan that morning. The morning of the christening. Seven weeks, and no heartbeat. Her husband was not parking. He was sitting in the car. She came anyway, because it was the only day that year the whole family would be in one room. And she stood up in the second row while the priest was pouring the water and she said it out loud, once, in front of everybody. So that her baby had been real to somebody other than her. She had the procedure on the Tuesday. I have told that story at four separate dinner parties. I was very funny about it. I always start it the same way.

title: She announced she was pregnant mid-christening, while the priest was pouring the water
description:
A hundred and forty people turned around. My daughter was eleven weeks old, in my grandmother's christening gown, and the priest actually stopped with the water still in his hand.

I was ready to hate her. She got engaged at my sister's engagement party — ask anyone in my family.

My aunt told me in November why she really did it.

Half the people in these comments will say she was wrong. The other half watched to the end.
